- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from high), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; use 7-day sentiment average to dampen noise.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast with sentiment trend only if sentiment is sustained >3 days.
- When true outcome is below 70, model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 75–80 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
